candidates.title: McDonald's ends 32-year FIFA World Cup sponsorship after its biggest-ever World Cup campaign; CMO: 'overly reliant on borrowed IP'
candidates.claim: Exit after 32 years (since 1994); 2026 campaign by Wieden+Kennedy NY in 110+ countries, largest marketing push of 2026; CFO Ian Borden (Q2 call): it 'provided a lift to the business' but 'underperformed versus our expectations'.
candidates.verification: verified: Adweek, Inside World Football, NRN/Restaurant Business, B&T, Marketing Dive read
candidates.notes: Corroborated by 4 more outlets. CMO Morgan Flatley quote 'overly reliant on borrowed IP' via NRN 2026-10-26. Adweek paywalled after intro.

candidates.title: What McDonald's FIFA exit means for sports marketing: rights are only the platform; activation costs $70-100M more
candidates.claim: Kantar: campaign lifted NPS and social buzz among young consumers; Q2 US same-store sales +0.8%, McDonald's attributed one-third of the traffic loss to the World Cup campaign; reportedly ~$80M committed for the 2026 cycle; SponsorUnited's Bob Lynch: 'the onus is on the brands'; shift to owned IP and many smaller deals.
candidates.verification: partly verified: analysis piece; '1/3 of traffic loss' and '$80M' are single-source (estimate/reported) — keep off screen
candidates.notes: Use as context, not headline numbers.

lenses_summary.verification_red_team: Exit, 32 years, 110+ countries, W+K, CFO 'underperformed versus our expectations' and Flatley 'overly reliant on borrowed IP' verified across Adweek/NRN/B&T/IWF/Marketing Dive. Do NOT claim the sponsorship 'failed' or 'lost money': CFO also said it 'provided a lift'. '$80M' is 'reportedly'; 'one-third of traffic loss' is single-source — caption only, labelled. Dates: Adweek exclusive 2026-10-23; other outlets report 25-26 Oct. Avoid FIFA governance/scandal angle (IWF mentions it; McDonald's says unrelated).
lenses_summary.audience_psychology: Every business owner has paid to stand next to something bigger (an exhibition booth, an influencer, a celebrity, an event). The sting: applause goes to the borrowed name; when the contract ends, nothing stays with you. Familiar World Cup + a giant walking away = high curiosity; the counter-intuitive beat is 'they quit after their BIGGEST campaign'.
lenses_summary.brand_fit: Squarely brand strategy (borrowed vs owned brand assets), Behnood's positioning as strategist; actionable for SMEs; no politics; works identically for Persian and international audiences (football is universal).

gates.brand_fit: pass: C1/C3/C12 merged; C4 fails repetition; C5 fails audience relevance; C11 fails verifiability
gates.story_gate: winner: C1+C3+C12 — tension 'biggest campaign ever, then they walked away'; concrete image: a row of nine cups, eight with borrowed star faces and one with their own character.

decision.why: Highest totals (C1 91, C3 91, C12 87); breaking news as spark, evergreen lesson (borrowed vs owned equity) as the body; strongest single image; fresh vs last 7 days.
